To find the characteristic polynomial of a matrix $A$, we compute the determinant of $\lambda I - A$, where $I$ is the identity matrix. Given the matrix $A$:
\[ 
A = \begin{pmatrix}
-4 & -13 & 10 \\
-9 & 10 & 4 \\
12 & -5 & -14
\end{pmatrix}
\]
We start by setting up the matrix $\lambda I - A$:
\[ 
\lambda I - A = 
\begin{pmatrix}
\lambda+4 & 13 & -10 \\
9 & \lambda-10 & -4 \\
-12 & 5 & \lambda+14
\end{pmatrix}
\]
Now, we find the determinant of this matrix using expansion along the first row (or any method preferred):
\[
\text{det}(\lambda I - A) = (\lambda + 4)\text{det}\left(\begin{pmatrix}
\lambda-10 & -4 \\
5 & \lambda+14
\end{pmatrix}\right) - 13\text{det}\left(\begin{pmatrix}
9 & -4 \\
-12 & \lambda+14
\end{pmatrix}\right) + (-10)\text{det}\left(\begin{pmatrix}
9 & \lambda-10 \\
-12 & 5
\end{pmatrix}\right)
\]
The determinant of each $2 \times 2$ matrix is:
\[
\text{det}\left(\begin{pmatrix}
\lambda-10 & -4 \\
5 & \lambda+14
\end{pmatrix}\right) = (\lambda - 10)(\lambda + 14) + 20 = \lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120 + 20 = \lambda^2 + 4\lambda -100
\]
\[
\text{det}\left(\begin{pmatrix}
9 & -4 \\
-12 & \lambda+14
\end{pmatrix}\right) = 9(\lambda + 14) - (-48) = 9\lambda + 126 + 48 = 9\lambda + 174
\]
\[
\text{det}\left(\begin{pmatrix}
9 & \lambda-10 \\
-12 & 5
\end{pmatrix}\right) = 9 \times 5 - (-12)(\lambda-10) = 45 + 12\lambda - 120 = 12\lambda - 75
\]
Substituting those into our expansion:

\[
\text{det}(\lambda I - A) = (\lambda + 4)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 100) - 13(9\lambda + 174) - 10(12\lambda - 75)
\]
\[
= \lambda^3 + 4\lambda^2 + 4\lambda^2 + 16\lambda - 100\lambda - 400 - 117\lambda - 2262 - 120\lambda + 750
\]
\[
= \lambda^3 + 8\lambda^2 - 337\lambda - 1912
\]

Thus, the characteristic polynomial of matrix $A$ is:
\[
\boxed{\lambda^3 + 8\lambda^2 - 337\lambda - 1912}
\]
